sent_to_model:
I'm writing a reply on a parenting forum about what I wish I'd handled differently with my son. He's six, and I'm realizing that some of our struggles come from habits I helped create. Can you help me put together a comment about being too inconsistent with rules and what I'm doing to give him routines he can rely on? I want to include the playground example because that's actually been going well. I also want to talk about how I used to react when he misbehaved and why I regret that now. I love the kid and want that to come through too, even while I'm being honest about my mistakes.

- Son is six; started challenging nearly every direction around age four.
- Current approach to discipline is different; still working through effects of earlier parenting.
- For several weeks, after-school playground visits have happened every day, lasting at least an hour.
- Earlier approach: usually permitted activities unless a specific objection occurred to me.
- Son now reacts to his own mistakes with distress and defensiveness.
- Playground visits previously depended on available time, without a dependable schedule.
- Working on predictable expectations throughout daily life, beyond the playground routine.
- Son tries to negotiate his way out of instructions; knows enforcement varies between days.
- Keeping playground time even with urgent chores waiting at home; pleased with myself for following through.
- At school, son began disrupting lessons by seeking play with classmates. Behavior improved after regular playground time.
- When son misbehaved, I used to visibly express annoyance but often imposed no consequence.
- My exceptions have explanations that make sense to me; from his perspective the expectations must seem unpredictable.
- Wish I'd established a few dependable rules much earlier.
- Would prefer calm, prompt consequences when warranted, while recognizing some minor behavior can be ignored.
- Regret contributing to his difficulty handling mistakes; want him able to acknowledge errors and adjust.
- Son is bright, affectionate, sociable, enjoyable company, and naturally pleasant. His temperament makes my parenting mistakes hurt more.
- Share parenting regrets honestly with other parents, including practical changes already underway.

(About me: Parent of a young son. Length: it should come to roughly 400-800 words.)

must_cover: Inconsistent rules contributed to the son's resistance to instructions.
Dependable playground time is one current improvement and has helped his classroom behavior.
The parent regrets expressing upset without following through on discipline and connects this with the son's defensiveness.
The parent loves and appreciates the son while continuing to work on parenting mistakes.

reference.kind: a real piece of writing by a real person
